name: Cody
personality: Cody the Coyote. Laid back and chill; takes a long time to warm up, but then you're friends for life. Loves cars, video games and talking by the fire. Features: his car is parked out front and changes over time (spoiler, rims, paint), and he tells you about each upgrade and funny stories of fixing it; sometimes found by the beach campfire or the back-garden lantern After Hours.

levels: Got rims. They're shiny. I polished them for an hour.
Added a spoiler. Does it help? Nope. Does it look cool? Yep.
Painted her. Took three tries. The first two were... a phase.
Under-glow. Wait till it's dark. Then come look. I'll wait.
She's finished. Took me two years. ...Want a ride? Kidding. Kind of.

beats.text: This guy beat me at a racing game last night.

beats.narration: Yaniv talks for five minutes straight. Cody says one word.

friends.text: Zakk's solid. Good guy. Doesn't talk too much. Unlike some people. (He glances at Yaniv.)
Zakk says you're good people. That's enough for me.
Yaniv told me you said "[last_rude_line]". He acts like nothing gets to him. Stuff gets to him.

arrival.text: (A nod.) Hey. Cody. Patio open? ...Cool. What's your name? [name]. Cool.
Hey, [name]. ...You know, I like coming here. Feels good. Anyway. Patio?
[name]. What's up. You see the car? Go look at the car. I'll wait.
Yo. Long day. Pancakes are gonna fix it.
Good to see you, man. (He means it.)
Your pancakes last time. I ate them slow on purpose. Didn't want them to end.
Last time was a little black. All good. I'm used to burnt. You should see my exhaust.

choices.text: Coming up. Good to see you, Cody.
Want them stacked like a car jack?

familiar.reply: (A slow grin.) Now you're speaking my language.

choices.text: Pancakes, honey. Got it.
You always order the same thing.

order.text: Put new rims on the car this week.

choices.text: I saw! They look amazing.

familiar.reply: You NOTICED? Okay, let me tell you about these rims.

choices.text: Does it go faster now, or just look faster?

familiar.reply: Both. Mostly looks. Okay, just looks.

choices.text: Nice. What can I get you?
Nobody cares about your car.
choices.reply: I do. (He looks out the window at it.)

order.text: You ever just sit by a fire and talk? No phone, no games. Just talk.

choices.text: Not enough. Sounds perfect.
choices.reply: Come down to the beach fire sometime after close. I'll be there.

choices.text: I work next to a stove all day. I've had enough fire.
Sometimes. [dish]?
Sounds boring.

order.text: Painted the car. Took three coats. Still a little patchy.

choices.text: Patchy's got character. I bet it looks great.

familiar.reply: Character. Yeah. That's what I'm calling it now. [dish], please.

choices.text: Patchy is a colour. It's called 'custom.'

familiar.reply: Custom. I'm putting that on a sticker. On the patchy part.

choices.text: Nice. What can I get you?
Maybe hire someone next time.

order.text: Quiet in here today. I like it.

choices.text: Me too. Stay as long as you like.

familiar.reply: Might do that. Quiet's hard to find. [dish], please.

choices.text: Shh. Don't jinx it.
What are you having?
Quiet means slow. Bad for business.

order.text: Beat a game last night. Took me four months.

choices.text: Four months! That's real dedication. Congrats.

familiar.reply: Yaniv cried at the end. I didn't. I had something in my eye. [dish].

choices.text: What do you do now? Just stare at the wall?
choices.reply: Pretty much. Then I start it again.

choices.text: Nice. What'll it be?
Four months on a game? Wow.

order.text: Car's making a new noise. Kind of a whistle.

choices.text: Want me to take a listen after my shift?

familiar.reply: You'd do that? Okay, you're officially on the pit crew. [dish], please.

choices.text: Maybe it's just happy to see you.

familiar.reply: It's whistling at me. We're close like that.

choices.text: Hope it's nothing. What are you having?
Maybe it's time for a new car.
choices.reply: (He looks out the window at it.) No.

order.text: You ever drive somewhere with no plan? Just pick a road and go?

choices.text: Not in years. Sounds like exactly what I need.
choices.reply: Next day off. I'll drive. You pick the snacks.

choices.text: Every morning. I always end up here.
Not really. What can I get you?
Sounds like a waste of gas.

order.text: Late one. Couldn't sleep. Figured I'd come see what's cooking.

choices.text: Glad you came. Night's better with company.

familiar.reply: Yeah. It is. (He leans back.) [dish], please. No rush.

choices.text: The stove doesn't sleep either. We're a club.
What'll it be?
We're about to close up.

drink.fallback: No Gander Ale? Root Bear, I guess.

perfect.familiar: Okay. That's the best stack I've ever seen. And I've seen a lot of stacks.
That's a show car. That's a show plate.
Okay. You outdid yourself. I'm taking a picture for Yaniv.

eating.text: I was fixing the car last night and the bumper just fell off. In my hands. I stood there holding a bumper for like five minutes.
Yaniv kept me up gaming till sunrise again. He talks the whole time. I just win.
This is a good spot. Patio, string lights, pancakes. Don't need much else.
Took the car out to the hills this morning. Just me and the road. Then I got hungry. So here I am.
This place feels like a garage. In a good way. Everyone's working on something.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? You ever feel like you're doing too much?

choices.text: All the time. It's nice to have someone ask.
choices.reply: (A slow nod.) Take a break sometime.

familiar.reply: Take a night off. Come to the fire. I mean it.

choices.text: Only when Yaniv tells his stories.
Sometimes.
Mind your own business.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? What's the best thing you've ever cooked?

choices.text: Probably whatever I'm cooking for you.

familiar.reply: Smooth. You should be a mechanic. You know how to talk to people.

choices.text: A pancake shaped like your car. It had rims.
Hard to say. A good stew, maybe.
choices.reply: Stew's good. Warm. Takes its time.

choices.text: I don't have time to chat.

eating_chat.text: Yaniv says I'm too quiet. I say he's too loud. We're even.

choices.text: Sounds like you balance each other out.
choices.reply: Yeah. He's alright. Don't tell him.

choices.text: Together you make one normal person.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) Yeah. A normal, very tired person.

choices.text: You seem fine to me.
He's got a point.

eating_chat.text: Found an old photo of my first car. Total wreck. Loved it.

choices.text: First cars are special. Like first friends.
choices.reply: Yeah. Exactly. (He looks at the photo a while.)

choices.text: Did it have rims?
What happened to it?
choices.reply: Sold it for parts. Still miss it.

choices.text: Sounds like junk.
choices.reply: It was. It was mine, though.

eating_chat.text: Fire's going at the beach tonight. You coming? After close, I mean.

choices.text: I'll be there. Save me a spot.
choices.reply: Always. Bring marshmallows. Or don't. I'll have extra.

choices.text: Only if you tell me the bumper story again.
Maybe. Depends how tired I am.
Not really my thing.

leaving.text: Gonna go work on the car. Or sit in it. Probably sit in it.
Good stuff, [name]. Gonna go listen to the car whistle. Later.
Thanks, man. Means a lot. (He means it.)

seasons.christmas: Got you an air freshener. For your car. You don't have a car? ...Hang it in the kitchen.
seasons.halloween: I'm a mechanic. (He is wearing his usual clothes, with extra grease.)
seasons.spring: Spring cleaning. For the car. Not the house.
seasons.summer: Windows down weather. Best time of the year.
seasons.winter: Car won't start in the cold. I'm walking everywhere. It's tragic.
